A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WAFT-Stereo and provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables supporting a reliable comparison. Both contain 19 pages, end with references, and contain no separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, training-data and architecture ablations, qualitative predictions, and inference-cost measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds first-step disparity-error measurements on ETH3D subsets.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same LoRA-adapted encoder, initial disparity classification, warping-based recurrent regression, high-resolution ResNet blocks, and classification-plus-MoL objective. The added explanation does not alter the method.

E1.justification: The training datasets and ETH3D, KITTI, and Middlebury evaluation coverage are retained. The new large-disparity breakdown analyzes existing ETH3D pixels; the revised training-pair count changes reported scale rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons in Tables 1–6 retain the same comparator methods and ablation variants. The additional related-work citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1 and 4.5 revise the stated SynLarge training pool from approximately 3.3 million to 7.7 million pairs, substantially changing the reported training-data scale while retaining the dataset list and 400k-step budget. This does not establish that experiments were rerun. Section 3.2 also adds first-step EPE evaluation restricted to ETH3D pixels with 40px+ and 50px+ disparities.

E4.justification: Section 3.2 adds a targeted analysis comparing classification and regression initialization on large-disparity ETH3D pixels. Existing training-data, disparity-bin, backbone, loss, and architectural ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The additional EPE results are point estimates.

E6.justification: Existing table values and plotted results are unchanged. Section 3.2 newly reports first-step EPE of 0.89 versus 1.11 for 40px+ disparities and 1.80 versus 2.88 for 50px+, comparing classification-plus-regression with regression-only initialization.

T1.justification: The warping definition, soft target distribution, cross-entropy loss, soft-argmax initialization, and total training objective are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies its previously unqualified first-place benchmark claim by specifying ETH3D BP-0.5, Middlebury RMSE, and KITTI all metrics. The central claims about cost-volume-free matching, efficiency, and generalization remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 adds that regression can initialize better on average while severely misestimating large-disparity pixels that remain stuck, explaining the benefit of classification. Existing discussions of SceneFlow overfitting and the Classroom2E illumination failure remain.

D1.justification: Training-data documentation revises the SynLarge volume from 3.3 million to 7.7 million pairs without explaining whether this corrects the earlier description or reflects changed experiments. Other implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and code/model access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Peng et al.'s Rethinking Depth Estimation for Multi-View Stereo and HITNet to the classification-related citations. It also removes MC-CNN from the direct-dense-prediction characterization while retaining that work elsewhere. The overall research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to the abstract, the expanded classification explanation, and terminology such as replacing qHD with 540p. The section sequence and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All six figures and six tables are retained. Figure 6 and Table 6 move from page 14 to page 15, surrounding text reflows, and the Figure 2 and Table 6 captions replace qHD with 540p. There is no substantive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 improves precision by identifying the winning metrics in the abstract and adds targeted evidence supporting classification on large-disparity pixels. Additional citations improve attribution. These are limited gains because the method and existing results remain unchanged, and the unexplained training-count revision leaves uncertainty about experimental provenance.
